description:
The private art and design school, Rome University of Fine Arts (RUFA), is located in Rome, at the heart of Italy. RUFA was founded in 1998 to achieve the dreams of its founder, Maestro Alfio Mongelli, as well as those of Italian and international students within a single academy. In addition to visual arts, design, cinema, photography, multimedia, theater, animation, and other fields of the arts, it offers a variety of programs in these areas. As part of its mission to prepare students for professions in the creative industries, RUFA is renowned for its emphasis on practical training and hands-on experience. RUFA offers Bachelor and Master of Arts degree programs that fully respond to current artistic and cultural contexts, offering the best possible training in the arts and solid, immediate job prospects. Therefore, RUFA is an excellent place to study the visual arts, and its reputation is well-deserved. With a strong emphasis on research and a vibrant student life, RUFA is a perfect choice for anyone interested in a career in the visual arts.

The Rome University of Fine Arts provides bachelor's and master's degree programs, and its curriculum often includes a mix of theoretical and practical courses. Students can work on projects, collaborate with peers, and engage with professionals from the artistic and creative fields. Living arrangements and housing options for students at the Rome University of Fine Arts (RUFA) can be diverse and fascinating. RUFA may provide on-campus or connected housing as a convenient option for students. Additionally, RUFA became a partner of the Spotahome platform, which operates throughout Europe and specializes in medium and long-term lodging. This will enable you to rent verified houses online in the city where your RUFA headquarters is situated, saving you time, energy, and money and allowing you to begin your career at the Academy as quickly as possible.  Many students, however, prefer to rent private apartments or share living quarters with housemates. Rent is a substantial expense in Rome, ranging from €700 to €1,200 for a single-bedroom apartment in the city center. Monthly costs include utilities, groceries, dining out, and transportation.

Rome's rich cultural heritage, world-renowned buildings, and gastronomic delights offer a one-of-a-kind cultural experience. While living conditions vary, Rome's solid cultural offerings make it an enticing city for students to live and study in. When planning your lodging in Rome, it is best to perform thorough research and examine your interests, and don't be afraid to get advice from RUFA about housing alternatives and living in the city. Additionally, you can reach out to us in order to get help on your journey.
